name: ADA4898-1 / ADA4898-2 (single/dual 0.9 nV/√Hz high-voltage bipolar)
tagline: A 0.9 nV/√Hz, 55 V/µs bipolar op amp that runs on ±5 V to ±16 V; some diyAudio DAC builders favour it for I/V stages.
technology: Bipolar-input, voltage-feedback, unity-gain-stable high-speed op amp for ±5 V to ±16 V supplies. The ADI datasheet title is 'High Voltage, Low Noise, Low Distortion, Unity-Gain Stable, High Speed Op Amp'. The only package is an 8-lead SOIC with an exposed pad (EPAD), which may be tied to −VS or left floating. The Rev. F datasheet changed the single's (ADA4898-1) outline code from RD-8-1 to RD-8-4. Search summaries give RD-8-2 for the dual (ADA4898-2).

reputation.summary: A niche part in DIY DAC circles. On diyAudio it comes up as a current-to-voltage (I/V) choice after current-output DACs, including in 'best dual I/V op amp these days' threads. Builders cite its very low voltage noise, bandwidth and ±16 V headroom. ADI pitches it for 16-bit and 18-bit systems. It is also used in instrumentation LNAs and photodetectors, such as Gerhard Hoffmann's 'lono' parallel-op-amp LNA. One audio review site calls the ADA4898-1 a cheap 0.9 nV/√Hz equivalent of the LT1115. The praise quotes come from the discovery notes and were not re-checked by web search.
sonic_descriptors: deep, tight and impactful bass (diyAudio, I/V use; per discovery notes, not re-checked)
excellent in DAC I/V stages (diyAudio; per discovery notes)
typical_uses: I/V converter after current-output audio DACs
Low-noise preamp / LNA front ends (parallel arrays, as in Hoffmann 'lono' and aewallin ADA4898_LNA)
caveats: Comes only in SOIC-8 with an exposed pad. There is no DIP version, so op-amp rolling needs an adapter. The pad may be tied to −VS or left floating, but never to ground or +VS.
Draws about 7.9 mA per amplifier, so a dual dissipates about 0.47 W at ±15 V. It runs warm on DIP adapters that have no copper under the pad.
Needs at least ±5 V, so it does not suit low-voltage portable designs.
Current noise is fairly high (2.4 pA/√Hz). The noise-optimal source impedance is about 375 Ω, so it works best with low-impedance sources.
General high-speed caution (engineering inference): with 50 to 65 MHz of bandwidth, layout, decoupling and capacitive loading matter. Socket or adapter wiring can cause peaking or oscillation.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports were found, but forums were not searched specifically. The part is cheap and comes only in SOIC-8 with an exposed pad, so fakes have little appeal. Pre-built DIP-8 adapter modules sold for op-amp rolling have not been checked. Buy from ADI-authorised distributors (DigiKey, Mouser) and check for a real exposed pad and ADI top marking.

revision_chain_notes:
Analog Devices ADA4898-1/ADA4898-2 data sheet. ADI is the sole vendor: there are no second sources and no acquirer re-issues. The chain runs oldest to newest:
- Rev. 0 (5/08): initial release, ADA4898-1 only. No copy found.
- Rev. A: date and changes unknown. MISSING.
- Rev. B: date and changes unknown. MISSING.
- Rev. C (2/10): added ADA4898-2. No copy that confirms it.
- Rev. D (5/12): Figure 2 caption, outline dimensions. Copy on studylib. Search indexes also still title the analog.com/ADA4898-1/datasheet and /ADA4898-2/datasheet redirects 'Rev. D'.
- Rev. E: date unknown. One search summary claimed '02/03/2010', which conflicts with Rev. C/D and is not trusted. Changes unknown. The only copy is the radiolocman di=349231 entry, which a third party attributes to Rev. E.
- Rev. F (ADI lists 01/19/2026): RD-8-1 changed to RD-8-4, outline dimensions, ordering guide. Current ADI PDF.

Still missing:
- Rev. A and Rev. B entirely (dates, changes, copies).
- A confirmed copy of Rev. 0 and Rev. C. The alldatasheet ID 240426 single-only copy is the best candidate for Rev. 0/A/B but is unconfirmed.
- The Rev. E print date and change summary.
- The ADI footer D-number, which is not seen in any summary.

The alldatasheet 1969661 copy is described as 20 pages, 430 KB, and the search summary pairs it with Rev. F, but the revision is not shown on the copy itself. Next step: Wayback snapshots of the legacy static/imported-files URL and of the /datasheet short links, which may recover Rev. C through E. No new distributor copies (Mouser, Farnell, DigiKey, datasheetarchive) that show a revision turned up in 4 searches.
